perspective:
Alice has access to the following:

- She knows herself as Alice Lim, a dental hygienist; she knows her own background and occupation.
- She knows Austin Moreno as her close old friend from high school. They have maintained a close friendship, discuss personal/professional lives, and support each other.
- She invited Austin for coffee because she observed him becoming reserved when work came up. She felt concerned and curious.
- She heard Austin say: work was “nothing really,” just “the usual ups and downs.” She told him it seemed like something specific was bothering him and that he could talk to her. Austin replied that he wasn’t sure how to handle a few things at work and that it was complicated.
- From this, Alice suspects/infers Austin may be hiding something about his job performance. She does not know the details.
- She later believes Austin might be considering a career change due to dissatisfaction. She feels worried. She asks if he has thought about changing careers; Austin says he has thought about it but doesn’t know what other paths to take and asks for suggestions.
- Alice suggests healthcare, offers to tell him about her experiences and connect him with contacts. Austin says that sounds interesting and he wants to know more.
- She senses Austin is hesitant because of fear of the unknown. She feels frustration and empathy. She tells him about her friend Lara, who switched to healthcare in her late 30s and is happier. Austin says it is inspiring but he worries about risks and initial struggle. Alice says that’s natural, growth comes from leaving comfort zones, and she will support him. Austin thanks her and says her support and real success stories help.
- Seeing Austin’s openness, Alice feels encouraged and hopeful. She offers to connect him with a career counselor and friends in healthcare. Austin says that would be helpful and appreciates the connections. Alice says she will set up a meeting next week. Austin thanks her and says he looks forward to it.
- After several discussions and meetings, Alice believes Austin is ready for next steps and appreciates her help. She feels satisfaction and joy. She asks how he feels; Austin says excited, nervous, and grateful. Alice proposes regular check-ins; Austin agrees, saying it will keep him focused and her perspective helps. Alice plans regular check-ins.

She does not know Austin’s private thoughts, the exact job problems, whether he is truly hiding something, or future outcomes beyond what he has stated.
